chunks: It is narrated that he lived until the days of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and his report is well known, for he said to him: Explain to me your lifespan.

He replied: I lived two hundred years during the interval (of the prophets) of Jesus, and one hundred and twenty years in the period of Ignorance, and sixty years in Islam. He said to him: You were sought by a luck that did not stumble. His stories are well known, and he is the one who said when he reached three hundred years: My youth has become thin, if it supports me, it has rested for an afternoon. The verses are well known. And he is the one who said: When it is winter, warm me, for winter destroys the old man. But when every cold goes away, a light trouser or a cloak suffices. When the youth lives for two hundred years, he has exhausted the pleasure and the youthfulness.
ai.seo_question: Who is Rabi' ibn Khuthayr and how long did he live according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narrative from Al-Ghayba attributes a lifespan of three hundred years to the poet Rabi' ibn Khuthayr, placing him as a contemporary of the Prophet Muhammad and extending his life into the Umayyad era of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. The account underscores the concept of *al-Jahiliyya* (the pre-Islamic era) as a distinct historical period that persisted for over a century after the Prophet's death, a view supported by Shia historiography. The inclusion of his poetry serves to humanize this extraordinary longevity, linking the physical decline of old age with the spiritual transition from ignorance to divine guidance.
